raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Add native ModelExpress weight-transfer backend support through `POST /update_weights_from_modelexpress`. Trainers can request a published weight version while SGLang delegates staging and installation to MX. This integration targets `main` and can be used by different training frameworks.

## Modifications

```text
version request → native weight-update lock → scheduler checks (PP, draft model)
                → TP workers: cache checks + MX stage → TP staging agreement
                → restore packed layers → MX apply → release
                → TP install agreement → record version → flush caches
```

- Use the native weight-update synchronization helper, including when generation is already paused.
- Delegate receiver configuration to MX's public `get_modelexpress_generator()`. `WeightUpdater` creates the optional client on the first refit, reuses it, and closes it at scheduler shutdown.
- Install only after every TP rank has staged the version. If any rank fails to stage, release the staged handles and fail without touching the weights. Combine every rank's install result before reporting success.
- Before installing, restore layers that a kernel repacked in place (compressed-tensors W4A16 MoE on Marlin, BF16 MoE on `flashinfer_trtllm`), as `begin_weight_update` does. Skip the restore when MX already serves the staged version, since MX does not reload it.
- Record the version as soon as the install succeeds, then flush the requested caches, as the other update paths do. A refused flush still fails the call.
- Reject pipeline parallelism, speculative draft models, and incompatible weight-cache modes before mutation, with a failed response (HTTP 400).
- Like the other update paths, record `weight_load_duration_seconds` under the `modelexpress` source, and clear the multimodal preprocess cache after a successful refit that flushes caches.
- Document installation from ModelExpress `main`, the upcoming v0.8.0 release, receiver configuration, and endpoint usage.

The validated workflow uses S3 deltas and full checkpoints, with transfer and reconstruction handled by MX. Companion implementation and trainer integration: [ModelExpress #826](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/pull/826) and [Miles #3886](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3886).

### Where to start

- [Model runner handler](https://github.com/nv-hwoo/sglang/blob/d334385c8ff89a200969fae7e2239e9626686a5a/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/weight_updater.py#L116): SDK delegation, TP staging and install agreement, the packed-layer restore, and staged-handle lifetime.
- [Scheduler handler](https://github.com/nv-hwoo/sglang/blob/d334385c8ff89a200969fae7e2239e9626686a5a/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py#L167): compatibility checks, version bookkeeping, cache flushing, and load timing.
- [Tokenizer handler](https://github.com/nv-hwoo/sglang/blob/d334385c8ff89a200969fae7e2239e9626686a5a/python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_control_mixin.py#L894): native synchronization, merged results, and multimodal cache clearing.
- [Handler tests](https://github.com/nv-hwoo/sglang/blob/d334385c8ff89a200969fae7e2239e9626686a5a/test/registered/unit/managers/test_modelexpress_handlers.py#L156): lifecycle, failure paths, TP agreement, and paused/unpaused generation.

## Accuracy Tests

- **36 focused handler tests passed**, including paused-generation locking, TP staging and install agreement, and the restore order. The compensated-mHC update guard test also covers this endpoint. Applicable pre-commit checks passed.
- Full E2E run `miles-20261103-084017-b5e084` on the rebased branches: Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16, Megatron TP2/PP2/EP2 on four B200 GPUs, SGLang TP4 on four B200 GPUs, AWS S3, 24 updates, and full checkpoints at updates 10 and 20.
- All 24 updates succeeded. Verified 25 READY catalog versions including the seed, S3 artifacts, changed stable-version GPU checksums, and final generation at version 24 with no mixed versions.
- Tested SGLang `main@751fa99d7e` plus this PR (`d334385c8f`), Miles `742c7879d` ([Miles #3886](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3886) on Miles `main@e8046accd`), and MX [`60f5c69cc207`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/commit/60f5c69cc2075d39136af77dcc6bafd50a659ad7), the final head of [ModelExpress #826](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/pull/826), merged to `main` as [`e865b20f27`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/commit/e865b20f2771f594b06dede75fc6ef0718af186e). Miles `main` does not yet run against SGLang `main`, so the E2E image patched two Miles argument-parsing functions; that validation-only change is in neither PR.
- Final generation used four training-dataset prompts. A held-out accuracy comparison between native loading and MX refit remains pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End-to-end weight-update times from the same run, including trainer staging, S3 publication, and receiver refit:

| Update type | Count | Mean |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| All deltas | 22 | 58.0 s |
| Deltas excluding the initial update and updates immediately after a full checkpoint | 19 | 41.6 s |
| Full checkpoints | 2 | 699.5 s |

The full updates took 692.1 s and 706.9 s. The earlier run on the pre-review code (`miles-20261028-190301-f46678`) measured 56.7 s, 41.6 s, and 735.1 s. See [Miles #3886 — Test and Validation](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3886) for earlier runs and observed rollout/decode throughput, with the tested source snapshots and workload details.

nodes.body: **[High] A staging failure on one rank leaves the TP group serving mixed weights.** Each rank runs `stage_weight` and then `apply_weight` on its own, and ranks only agree after installation (line 131). If one rank's staging fails (S3 error, timeout, local disk) while the others succeed, those ranks install version N and the failed rank stays on N-1. The call reports failure, but there is no rollback (the disk path reloads the original weights), so the TP group is left with mixed weights. Suggest all-gathering the staging result before `apply_weight`, and releasing the staged handle on every rank if any rank failed.

detail.body:
## Motivation

Add native ModelExpress weight-transfer backend support through `POST /update_weights_from_modelexpress`. Trainers can request a published weight version while SGLang delegates staging and installation to MX. This integration targets `main` and can be used by different training frameworks.

## Modifications

```text
version request → native weight-update lock → scheduler checks (PP, draft model)
                → TP workers: cache checks + MX stage → TP staging agreement
                → restore packed layers → MX apply → release
                → TP install agreement → record version → flush caches
```

- Use the native weight-update synchronization helper, including when generation is already paused.
- Delegate receiver configuration to MX's public `get_modelexpress_generator()`. `WeightUpdater` creates the optional client on the first refit, reuses it, and closes it at scheduler shutdown.
- Install only after every TP rank has staged the version. If any rank fails to stage, release the staged handles and fail without touching the weights. Combine every rank's install result before reporting success.
- Before installing, restore layers that a kernel repacked in place (compressed-tensors W4A16 MoE on Marlin, BF16 MoE on `flashinfer_trtllm`), as `begin_weight_update` does. Skip the restore when MX already serves the staged version, since MX does not reload it.
- Record the version as soon as the install succeeds, then flush the requested caches, as the other update paths do. A refused flush still fails the call.
- Reject pipeline parallelism, speculative draft models, and incompatible weight-cache modes before mutation, with a failed response (HTTP 400).
- Like the other update paths, record `weight_load_duration_seconds` under the `modelexpress` source, and clear the multimodal preprocess cache after a successful refit that flushes caches.
- Document installation from ModelExpress `main`, the upcoming v0.8.0 release, receiver configuration, and endpoint usage.

The validated workflow uses S3 deltas and full checkpoints, with transfer and reconstruction handled by MX. Companion implementation and trainer integration: [ModelExpress #826](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/pull/826) and [Miles #3886](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3886).

### Where to start

- [Model runner handler](https://github.com/nv-hwoo/sglang/blob/d334385c8ff89a200969fae7e2239e9626686a5a/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/weight_updater.py#L116): SDK delegation, TP staging and install agreement, the packed-layer restore, and staged-handle lifetime.
- [Scheduler handler](https://github.com/nv-hwoo/sglang/blob/d334385c8ff89a200969fae7e2239e9626686a5a/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py#L167): compatibility checks, version bookkeeping, cache flushing, and load timing.
- [Tokenizer handler](https://github.com/nv-hwoo/sglang/blob/d334385c8ff89a200969fae7e2239e9626686a5a/python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_control_mixin.py#L894): native synchronization, merged results, and multimodal cache clearing.
- [Handler tests](https://github.com/nv-hwoo/sglang/blob/d334385c8ff89a200969fae7e2239e9626686a5a/test/registered/unit/managers/test_modelexpress_handlers.py#L156): lifecycle, failure paths, TP agreement, and paused/unpaused generation.

## Accuracy Tests

- **36 focused handler tests passed**, including paused-generation locking, TP staging and install agreement, and the restore order. The compensated-mHC update guard test also covers this endpoint. Applicable pre-commit checks passed.
- Full E2E run `miles-20261103-084017-b5e084` on the rebased branches: Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16, Megatron TP2/PP2/EP2 on four B200 GPUs, SGLang TP4 on four B200 GPUs, AWS S3, 24 updates, and full checkpoints at updates 10 and 20.
- All 24 updates succeeded. Verified 25 READY catalog versions including the seed, S3 artifacts, changed stable-version GPU checksums, and final generation at version 24 with no mixed versions.
- Tested SGLang `main@751fa99d7e` plus this PR (`d334385c8f`), Miles `742c7879d` ([Miles #3886](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3886) on Miles `main@e8046accd`), and MX [`60f5c69cc207`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/commit/60f5c69cc2075d39136af77dcc6bafd50a659ad7), the final head of [ModelExpress #826](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/pull/826), merged to `main` as [`e865b20f27`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/commit/e865b20f2771f594b06dede75fc6ef0718af186e). Miles `main` does not yet run against SGLang `main`, so the E2E image patched two Miles argument-parsing functions; that validation-only change is in neither PR.
- Final generation used four training-dataset prompts. A held-out accuracy comparison between native loading and MX refit remains pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End-to-end weight-update times from the same run, including trainer staging, S3 publication, and receiver refit:

| Update type | Count | Mean |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| All deltas | 22 | 58.0 s |
| Deltas excluding the initial update and updates immediately after a full checkpoint | 19 | 41.6 s |
| Full checkpoints | 2 | 699.5 s |

The full updates took 692.1 s and 706.9 s. The earlier run on the pre-review code (`miles-20261028-190301-f46678`) measured 56.7 s, 41.6 s, and 735.1 s. See [Miles #3886 — Test and Validation](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/3886) for earlier runs and observed rollout/decode throughput, with the tested source snapshots and workload details.

@@ -328,6 +329,72 @@ This path trades some I/O overhead for simplicity and flexibility. It integrates
 
 > **Note:** The diffusion engine (SGLang-Diffusion) does not currently support hot refit (updating weights while inference is in progress). The diffusion scheduler processes one request at a time and completes the entire inference before handling the next request, so weight updates and inference never run concurrently.
 
+### Update weights from ModelExpress
+
+Use ModelExpress (MX) to refit from a published S3 delta or full checkpoint. MX reconstructs the checkpoint locally and installs it through SGLang's model loader.
+
+**Prerequisites:**
+
+- Install ModelExpress from the current `main` branch in each worker environment:
+
+  ```bash
+  uv pip install "git+https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress@main#subdirectory=modelexpress_client/python"
+  ```
+
+- Give the workers access to the MX server, S3 credentials, and a writable checkpoint cache directory.
+
+<Note>
+ModelExpress v0.8.0 is coming soon and will include this support. Once released, you can `pip install modelexpress` v0.8.0 instead of installing from `main`.
+</Note>
+
+This example uses Linux with NVIDIA CUDA, a local Hugging Face checkpoint for `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B`, and tensor parallelism across four GPUs:
+
+```bash
+export MX_GENERATOR_SOURCE_ORDER=OBJECT_STORAGE
+
+python -m sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path /models/Qwen3-30B-A3B \
+  --tp-size 4 \
+  --modelexpress-config '{
+    "model_name": "Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B",
+    "server_url": "modelexpress:8001",
+    "initial_base_version_id": "v0",
+    "seed_checkpoint_path": "/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B",
+    "refit_checkpoint_dir": "/var/cache/modelexpress",
+    "object_storage_region_name": "us-west-2"
+  }'
+```
+
+For an S3-compatible service, also set `object_storage_endpoint_url` in this JSON configuration. S3 credentials use the standard AWS credential chain.
+
+**Endpoint:** `POST /update_weights_from_modelexpress`
+
+| Field | Description | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| `weight_version` | Opaque ID of the published MX version to install. | Required |
+| `flush_cache` | Flush serving caches after a successful update. | `true` |
+| `torch_empty_cache` | Also release unused CUDA allocator memory when flushing caches. | `false` |
+
+After the trainer publishes a READY version, pause generation, flush caches, refit, and resume. Replace `v1` with the published version ID:
+
+```python
+import requests
+
+server_url = "http://127.0.0.1:30000"
+for endpoint, payload in (
+    ("pause_generation", {"mode": "abort"}),
+    ("flush_cache", {}),
+    ("update_weights_from_modelexpress", {"weight_version": "v1", "flush_cache": False}),
+    ("continue_generation", {}),
+):
+    response = requests.post(f"{server_url}/{endpoint}", json=payload, timeout=900)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+```
+
+The explicit cache flush runs while generation is paused; `flush_cache=False` avoids flushing twice. The refit response contains `success` and `message`. The server records the installed version after all tensor-parallel workers succeed. Pipeline parallelism, speculative draft models, and incompatible shared or derived weight-cache modes are rejected.
+
+For trainer publication and cache settings, see the [ModelExpress S3 refit guide](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/modelexpress/blob/0af7e9e4438394588710b8b213cafec5e78db8de/docs/S3_DELTA_WEIGHT_REFIT.md#sglang-backend).
+
 ### Weight Update Session
 
 `update_weights_from_tensor` and `update_weights_from_distributed` must run inside a weight-update session. The update calls only write checkpoint-format values; `end_weight_update` runs every quantized layer's `process_weights_after_loading` once, turning them into kernel layout (Marlin repack, MXFP8 shuffles, ...), and runs `post_load_weights` if no weights were loaded through the engine during the session (P2P/RDMA writes). `begin_weight_update` first restores the few schemes whose kernel layout changes parameter shapes (today compressed-tensors W4A16 MoE on Marlin, and BF16 MoE on `flashinfer_trtllm` / `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`) so the checkpoint-format values fit. One session can span many update calls, so the finalize cost is paid once per refit rather than once per bucket. A call outside a session, a second `begin_weight_update`, or an `end_weight_update` without one is rejected with `success: false` (HTTP 400) and leaves the weights untouched.

+class Staged:
+    def __init__(self, version_id):
+        self.version_id = version_id
+        self.applied = False
+        self.released = 0
+        self.release_error = None
+        self.metrics = {}

+    def release(self):

+class Generator:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.worker_id = "generator-a"
+        self.staged = []
+        self.applied = []
+        self.closed = 0
+        self.stage_error = None
+        self.apply_error = None
+        self.release_error = None
+        self.serving_version = None
+
+    def stage_weight(self, *, version):
+        if self.stage_error is not None:
+            raise self.stage_error
+        if self.staged and not self.staged[-1].released:
+            staged = self.staged[-1]
+            if staged.version_id != version.version_id:
+                raise RuntimeError("another generator update is still active")
+            return staged
+        staged = Staged(version.version_id)
+        # MX returns an already-applied handle for the version it serves.
+        staged.applied = version.version_id == self.serving_version
+        staged.release_error = self.release_error
+        self.staged.append(staged)
+        return staged
+
+    def apply_weight(self, staged):
+        if self.apply_error is not None:
+            raise self.apply_error
+        self.applied.append(staged)
+
+    def close(self):
+        self.closed += 1
